t: How to Win Friends and Influence People
pitch: The great classic of human relations: don't criticize, take a genuine interest in others, persuade without confrontation, lead without hurting.
br: Start from what the other wants
point of view · interest · arouse desire
win an argument · lose the person
Getting the other to say yes
friendly tone · yes · let them talk · their idea
praise first · indirect · your own mistakes
quiz: Criticism puts people on the defensive without changing their behavior.
What's the difference between appreciation and flattery?
Appreciation is sincere and specific; flattery is false and self-serving
Flattery is quickly unmasked; sincere appreciation is rare and precious.
What does “start from what the other wants” mean?
Give in to all their demands
Show how what you propose meets what they want
You don't bait the hook with what you like, but with what the fish likes.
According to Carnegie, how do you win an argument?
Winning an argument means losing the other person's goodwill.
What should you do when you are wrong?
Wait for it to be forgotten
Admitting your fault before being reproached disarms the other.
What does Carnegie advise to be liked in conversation?
Listen and encourage the other to talk about themselves
People mostly appreciate those who listen to them.
How do you correct someone without hurting them?
Start with sincere praise and mention your own mistakes
And let the other person save face.
What does “give them a fine reputation to live up to” mean?
Express confidence in their abilities so they try to deserve it
People tend to act to live up to the image others have of them.
